parole.significato: A daughter-in-law or sister-in-law, especially one who lives with her husband's family when married.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi बहू (bahū) / Urdu بَہُو (bahū), from Sanskrit वधू (vadhū́).

parole.significato: A boxy building with twelve doors designed for free flow of air and excellent acoustics; similar buildings and pavilion…
parole.testo: From Hindi बारादरी (bārādrī) and Urdu بارہ دری (bārɘdɘrī), from बारह (bārah) and بارہ (bārā, bārah, “twelve”) + दर (dar) and دَر (dar, “door”).

parole.significato: A loose robe made from a single cloth, worn as a combination head covering, veil and shawl by chiefly Muslim women (and…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चादर (cādar) / Urdu چادَر (cādar), from Classical Persian چَادُر (čādur) or چَادَر (čādar), from Sanskrit छत्त्र (chattra). Doublet of chatra and chatta. Spelling possibly influenced by modern Iranian Persian چادُر (čâdor) or another language.

parole.significato: An official form or other kind of document, piece of paperwork, citation etc.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चालान (cālān) / Urdu چَالَان (cālān).

parole.significato: Prison.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चौकी (caukī) and Urdu چَوکی (caukī, “post, police station, etc.”).

parole.significato: A device used in India for drawing water from wells and discharging it into irrigation channels by means of pulley rope…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi चरसा (carsā) / Urdu چَرْسا (carsā)

parole.significato: An officer tasked with the administration of a sarkar.
parole.testo: From Hindi फ़ौजदार (faujdār)/Urdu فوجدار, from Persian فوجدار (fowj-dâr), compound of فوج (fowj, “troop”) (from Arabic فَوْج (fawj, “group”)) and ـدار (-dâr).

parole.significato: A clepsydra or water clock, consisting of a floating cup with a small hole in it, adjusted so that it fills and sinks i…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi घड़ी (ghaṛī) or Urdu گھڑی (ghaṛī).

parole.significato: A native Indian clerk or steward.
parole.testo: From Hindi [Term?], Urdu [Term?], from Persian گماشته (“appointed, delegated”).

parole.significato: A unit of length used in parts of Asia, ranging from 24 to 41 inches and historically used for measuring textiles, comp…
parole.testo: From Hindi गज़ (gaz) and Urdu گز (gaz), from Classical Persian گز (gaz). Doublet of gudge.

parole.significato: A type of private mansion in India and Pakistan.
parole.testo: Derived from Hindi हवेली (havelī) or Urdu حَویلی (havelī).

parole.significato: A type of cotton cloth, especially as dyed and waterproofed.
parole.testo: From Hindi जगन्नाथ (jagannāth) / Urdu جگنّاتھ (jagannāth), former name of Puri in India, where the material came from. Compare juggernaut.

parole.significato: A camel-borne pannier, litter, or cacolet.
parole.testo: From Hindi कजावा (kajāvā), from Urdu and Classical Persian کجاوه (kajāwa, “kajawah, howdah”).

parole.significato: The seeds of the plant Nigella sativa used as a spice.
parole.testo: From Hindi कलौंजी (kalauñjī) or कलोंजी (kaloñjī), Urdu کلونجی (kaloñjī).Which is ultimately derived from Tamil Karuñcīrakam(கருஞ்சீரகம்), black cumin.

parole.significato: A khapra beetle.
parole.testo: From Hindi [Term?] and/or Urdu [Term?] (“destroyer”).

parole.significato: A sweet rice pudding from South Asia.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi खीर / Urdu کھیر (khīr, “kheer”) (or a similar Indo-Aryan cognate), from Sanskrit क्षीर (kṣīrá, “milk”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *kšiHrám.

parole.significato: News.
parole.testo: From Hindi ख़बर (xabar) / Urdu خَبَر (xabar), from Persian خبر, from Arabic خَبَر (ḵabar). Doublet of gabber.

parole.significato: A flavoured frozen dessert of South Asia, made from milk and resembling ice cream.
parole.testo: From Hindi क़ुल्फ़ी (qulfī)/Urdu قلفی (qulfī), from Classical Persian قفلی (quflī) from قفل (qufl), from Arabic قُفْل (qufl, “lock, bolt”).

parole.significato: A traditional article of clothing worn in Afghanistan, Bangladesh, India, Pakistan, and Sri Lanka, consisting of a loos…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi कुरता (kurtā)/Urdu کرتا (kurtā), from Classical Persian کرته (kurta).

parole.significato: A spherical pot, specifically a water pot used for washing and ablution, typically made of brass.
parole.testo: From Hindi लोटा (loṭā) / Urdu لوٹا (loṭā). (person who switches loyalties): From the fact that the lota pot has a tendency to fall over and roll around, as it is not stable sitting on its base.

parole.significato: A garment worn around the waist, especially by men, in Southern India, Bangladesh, Burma, and Pakistan.
parole.testo: From Hindi लुंगी (luṅgī)/Urdu لنگی (lungī).

parole.significato: An elephant trainer, keeper, and driver.
parole.testo: PIE word  *méǵh₂s The noun is borrowed from Hindustani (Hindi महौत (mahaut)/Urdu مَہَوت (mahaut)), महाउत (mahāut), variants of महावत (mahāvat)/مَہاوَت (mahāvat), from Sanskrit महामात्र (mahāmātra, “elephant keeper; high official; king’s minister”), from महा (mahā, “great”) (ultimately from Proto-Ind

parole.significato: A part of a house or palace reserved for men, especially on the Indian subcontinent.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi मर्दाना (mardānā) / Urdu مردانہ (mardāna), from Persian مردانه (mardâne).

parole.significato: A South Asian beverage of black tea brewed in milk and water and then sweetened with sugar, with the addition of aromat…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi मसाला चाय (masālā cāy) / Urdu مصالہ چای (masālā cāy, literally “spiced/seasoned tea”).

parole.significato: A large crocodile, Crocodylus palustris, of southwest Asia, having a very broad wrinkled snout.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi मगर (magar) / Urdu مَگَر (magar, “crocodile, alligator”), from Sanskrit मकर (makara, “sea monster”), ultimately from Proto-Dravidian *nek-V-ḷ- (“crocodile”) (DEDR 3732; reconstruction of Krishnamurti 2003) or Proto-Dravidian *mokaray- (“crocodile”), a verbal noun from *mok- / *mo

parole.significato: One of the South and East Asian birds of the starling family Sturnidae.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi मैना (mainā) / Urdu مینا (mainā), from Sanskrit मदन (madana).

parole.significato: A type of round, flat bread baked in a tandoor popular in South and Central Asian cuisine.
parole.testo: From Hindi नान (nān) / Urdu نان (nān), from Classical Persian نان (nān), from Middle Persian LHMA (nān, “bread, food”).

parole.significato: A system of patrolling streets by use of checkpoints.
parole.testo: From Hindi नाकाबन्दी (nākābandī) and Urdu ناکابندی (nākā-bandī, “blockade, roadblock”).

parole.significato: A Muslim official in South Asia acting as a provincial deputy ruler under the Mughal empire; a local governor.
parole.testo: From Hindi नवाब (navāb)/Urdu نواب (navāb), from Persian نوّاب (navvâb), ultimately from Arabic نُوَّاب (nuwwāb), plural of نَائِب (nāʔib, “naib”).

parole.significato: Azadirachta indica, a large, mostly evergreen tree from India, whose seeds yield neem oil, the insecticide azadirachtin.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi नीम (nīm) / Urdu نِیم (nīm), from Sanskrit निम्ब (nimba).

parole.significato: A subdivision of currency, equal to one hundredth of a Indian, Nepalese, or Pakistani rupee.
parole.testo: From Hindi पैसा (paisā) / Urdu پَیسَہ (paisa), from Sauraseni Prakrit *𑀧𑀬𑀁𑀲 (*payaṃsa), presumably from unattested Sanskrit *पदांश (*padāṃśa), from पद (pada, “quarter”) + अंश (aṃśa, “part, piece”) in reference its historical value of ¹⁄₄ anna.

parole.significato: The sacred fig, Ficus religiosa.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi पीपल / Urdu پیپل (pīpal), from Sanskrit पिप्पल (pippala). Doublet of falafel and pepper.

parole.significato: A beverage, generally containing a mixture of fruit juice and some other beverage, often alcoholic.
parole.testo: PIE word  *pénkʷe From Hindi पाँच (pā̃c, “five”)/Urdu پانچ (pānc), because of the drink's original five ingredients (spirits, water, lemon juice, sugar, and spice), from Sanskrit पञ्च (páñca). Doublet of cinque, fin (“five currency units”), finnuf, five, pimp (“five”), ponzu, and sengi (“currency”);

parole.significato: A Hindu prince or ruler in India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi राजा (rājā) and Urdu راجا (rājā), from Sanskrit राजन् (rājan, “king, prince”), from Proto-Indo-Aryan *Hrā́ȷ́ā (“king”), from Proto-Indo-Iranian *Hrā́ȷ́ā, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃rḗǵ-ō, from *h₃rḗǵs (“ruler, king”). Doublet of Rex, rex, and roy.

parole.significato: A question-and-answer style correspondence between early modern South Asian and Iranian Zoroastrians, typically address…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi रिवायत (rivāyat) or Urdu رِوایَت (rivāyat), Persian روایت (revâyat), ultimately from Arabic رِوَايَة (riwāya, “narration”).

parole.significato: A kind of unleavened flatbread commonly consumed in South Asia and the Caribbean.
parole.testo: From Hindi रोटी (roṭī)/Urdu روٹی (roṭī), from Sanskrit रोटिका (roṭikā, “bread”).

parole.significato: A garden, especially one at a mausoleum.
parole.testo: From Hindi रौज़ा (rauzā, “garden; mausoleum”)/Urdu روضہ (rauza), from Classical Persian روضه (rawza), from Arabic روضة (rawḍa, “garden; meadow”).

parole.significato: A farmer or tiller of the soil.
parole.testo: 17th century. From Hindi रैयत (raiyat, “peasant”), from Urdu رعیت (ra'iyat, “peasant”), from Classical Persian رَعِیَّت (ra'iyyat, “population, peasants”), from Arabic رَعِيَّة (raʕiyya, “flock, herd”).

parole.significato: An administrative unit used mostly in the Muslim states of South Asia.
parole.testo: From Hindi सरकार (sarkār)/Urdu سرکار (sarkār), from Persian سرکار (sarkâr, “superintendent, overseer, chief”), compound of سر (sar, “head”) + کار (kâr, “agent, doer”).

parole.significato: The elected head of a panchayat (village government) in Bangladesh, India, or Pakistan.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi सरपंच (sarpañc), from Hindi सर (sar, “head”) / Urdu سر (sar, “head; chief”) (from Persian سر (sar, “head; chief, leader”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ḱerh₂- (“head; top”)) + Hindi पंच (pañc, “five (number of people in a panchayat council)”) / Urdu پنچ (pañc); from Sansk

parole.significato: Synonym of wedding.
parole.testo: From Hindi शादी (śādī) and Urdu شادی (śādī, “wedding; marriage”), from Persian شادی (šādī, “joy; rejoicing; wedding”), q.v.

parole.significato: Loose trousers worn in some South Asian or Islamic countries, especially by women but also by men, especially with a ka…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi शलवार (śalvār)/सलवार (salvār) or Urdu شَلْوار (śalvār)/سَلْوار (salvār), from Classical Persian شَلْوَار (šalwār).

parole.significato: meek, gentle, gentlemanly, upstanding, innocent
parole.testo: From Hindi शरीफ़ (śarīf)/Urdu شریف, from Arabic شَرِيف (šarīf).

parole.significato: A leguminous tree (Dalbergia sissoo) of northern India.
parole.testo: From Hindi [Term?] / Urdu [Term?]. Doublet of shisham.

parole.significato: A Hindustani/Indian classical stringed instrument, typically having a gourd as its resonating chamber.
parole.testo: From Hindi सितार (sitār) / Urdu ستار (sitār), from Classical Persian سهتار (si-tār, literally “three strings”). Doublet of setar.

parole.significato: A preparation of antimony with which Muslim men historically anointed their eyelids.
parole.testo: From Hindi सुरमा (surmā) / Urdu سرمہ (surmā), from Classical Persian سرمه (surma).

parole.significato: The governor or commander in charge of a subah; a viceroy.
parole.testo: From Hindi सूबेदार (sūbedār) / Urdu صوبدار (sūbadār), and its source, (Indian) Persian صوبهدار (sūbadār), corresponding to صوبه (sūba, “province”) + ـدار (-dār, “in ownership of, in charge of”).

parole.significato: A soft cake made with semolina flour and a high concentration of egg yolks, part of Eurasian, Malay, and Chinese cuisin…
parole.testo: The first element is cognate with English suji, ultimately from Hindi सूजी / Urdu سوجی (sūjī).

parole.significato: Wheat that is granulated but not pulverized; a kind of semolina.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi सूजी / Urdu سوجی (sūjī).

parole.significato: A rapid melodic vocal technique in raga singing.
parole.testo: From Hindi तान (tān)/Urdu تان (tān).

parole.significato: An administrative division in India and Pakistan.
parole.testo: From Hindi तहसील (tahsīl) and Urdu تحصیل.

parole.significato: An official reminder.
parole.testo: From Hindi ताकीद (tākīd) / Urdu تَاکِیدْ (tākīd), from Arabic تَأْكِيد (taʔkīd).

parole.significato: spectator; onlooker; sightseer
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi तमाशबीन (tamāśbīn)/Urdu تماشبین. From तमाशा (tamāśā, “spectacle”) + -बीन (-bīn, suffix concerning vision), from Persian تماشا + بین.

parole.significato: An amulet or locket containing verses from the Qur'an or other Islamic prayers and symbols.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi तावीज़ (tāvīz) / Urdu تَعْوِیذ (taʻwīẕ, taʻvīẕ), from Arabic تَعْوِيذ (taʕwīḏ)

parole.significato: Originally, a three-legged decorative stand or table; now, especially, one with recesses for holding tea caddies and/or…
parole.testo: PIE word  *tréyes Borrowed from Hindi तिपाई (tipāī), Urdu تپائی (tipāi, “teapoy”), from a merger of Sanskrit त्रिपाद (tripāda, “tripod”) + Classical Persian سه پای (sih-pāy, “tripod”), with the spelling of the first element influenced by association with tea. Sanskrit त्रि (tri, “three”), the first

parole.significato: An alcoholic drink of North India and Pakistan, made from yeast fermentation of sugar cane or wheat husk, and often bre…
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi ठर्रा (ṭharrā) / Urdu ٹَھرّا (ṭharrā).

parole.significato: A unit of mass used in India, equal to the mass of a silver rupee coin, fixed at 180 troy grains (11.663 8038 grams) in…
parole.testo: From Hindi तोला (tolā)/Urdu تولا (tolā), from Sanskrit तोलक (tolaka), from तोलः (tol, “weighing”) (root: तुल् (tul, “to weigh”)).

parole.significato: A pith helmet.
parole.testo: From Hindi टोपी (ṭopī)/Urdu ٹوپی (ṭōpī).

parole.significato: A feather-like ornament projecting from a tied turban.
parole.testo: From Hindi/Urdu, from Persian طره (torre).

parole.significato: A pool in a mosque where worshippers wash themselves, as part of wudu, before praying.
parole.testo: From Hindi वज़ूख़ाना (vazūxānā) / Urdu وضو خانہ (vazū-xānā, “washing room”), from वज़ू (vazū) / وضو (vazū, “washing, wudu”) + ख़ाना (xānā) / خانہ (xānā, “room”).

parole.significato: A small cannon supported by a swiveled rest, especially as mounted on the back of a camel.
parole.testo: From Hindi ज़ंबूरक (zambūrak) / Urdu زنبورک (zambūrak), from Classical Persian زنبورک (zanbūrak), from زنبور (zanbūr, “hornet”), from Arabic زُنْبُور (zunbūr, “hornet”).

parole.significato: The flavoured tobacco used in paan.
parole.testo: Hindi ज़र्दा (zardā); Urdu زردہ.

parole.significato: cumin
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi जीरा (jīrā)/Urdu زیرہ (zīra), from Sanskrit जीरक (Jīraka) or Classical Persian زیرہ (zīra).

parole.significato: Synonym of harem (“area of house or palace for high-caste women or wives of a wealthy man; the women thus kept; the sys…
parole.testo: From Hindi ज़नाना (zanānā), Urdu زنانه (zanānah), from Classical Persian زنانه (zanāna, “womanly”), from زن (zan, “woman”). Related to Old English cwene (“woman”). More at quean.

parole.significato: A district or local division, as of a province, in India.
parole.testo: Borrowed from Hindi ज़िला (zilā) and Urdu ضلع (zilā), from Classical Persian ضلع (zil', “side, edge”), from Arabic ضِلْع (ḍilʕ, “side, edge, division”). Cognate with Nepali जिल्ला (jillā) and Marathi जिल्हा (jilhā).
